title: Ideal transformer turns ratio and reflected load
description: Predict secondary RMS voltage and the primary-referred resistive load from winding turns.
formula: a = Ns/Np; Vs = a Vp; Rprimary = Rload/a²
assumptions: Ideal, lossless, perfectly coupled transformer in steady alternating excitation; no DC operation.
Neglect magnetizing current, leakage, winding resistance, regulation and saturation.
Voltages are RMS magnitudes; winding polarity is not represented. Load is purely resistive.
Reflected resistance uses sequential division by the turns ratio to avoid premature overflow or underflow of its square; this does not change the ideal model.

references.title: Stanford EE102 exercises, static-circuit exercise 10: Reflected resistance

constraints.message: Primary turns must be a positive integer
Secondary turns must be a positive integer

title: Rectangular-section toroid inductance
description: Integrate the radial 1/r field in an ungapped toroid rather than using a mean-radius approximation.
formula: L = mu0 mur N² h ln(ro/ri)/(2 pi); Binner = mu0 mur N Ipk/(2 pi ri)
assumptions: Toroid has rectangular radial/axial cross section, homogeneous real constant permeability and no discrete gap.
An evenly distributed winding confines flux to the toroid; leakage, winding self-capacitance and core losses are ignored.
Permeability is valid throughout the operating field range; inner-radius field is the highest field and is checked against a user-supplied linearity limit.
Use mu0 = 4 pi times 1e-7 H/m as an engineering approximation; dimensions are core radii, not diameters.

references.title: MIT 8.02 Spring 2003, Inductance Worked Examples, example 2: Rectangular-section toroid
MIT 6.014 Lecture 11, sections A and C: Linear magnetic material and toroidal inductors

outputs.label: Peak field at core inner radius

title: Finite-permeability gapped-core inductance
description: Estimate inductance with both core and total air-gap reluctance retained and check peak core flux.
formula: Rc = lc/(mu0 mur w h); Rg = g/(mu0 w h); L = N²/(Rc+Rg); Bpk = N Ipk/((Rc+Rg) w h)
assumptions: Single series magnetic path with uniform rectangular cross section; core length excludes air gaps and gap input is the total series gap length.
Homogeneous linear core, negligible leakage/fringing, equal core and gap flux areas; no parallel return paths.
The catalog conservatively requires total gap <= 0.1 times the smaller pole dimension and <= 0.1 times core path length. This is an approximation-screening rule, not an error guarantee or standard.
Peak flux must remain below the user-supplied linearity limit. Real fringing and bias-dependent permeability need manufacturer data or field analysis.
Use mu0 = 4 pi times 1e-7 H/m; no gap-dominant approximation is imposed.

references.title: MIT Electromagnetic Fields and Energy, section 9.7, example 9.7.1: Finite-permeability air-gap field
MIT 6.014 Lecture 11, section C: Gap, flux continuity and inductance

inputs.label: Core magnetic path length excluding gaps

title: Good-conductor skin depth
description: Calculate the 1/e penetration depth of a sinusoidal field in a good conductor and enforce a conduction-dominant domain.
formula: delta = sqrt(1/(pi f mu0 mur sigma)); require sigma/(2 pi f eps0 epsr) >= 100
assumptions: Homogeneous isotropic conductor with real, positive, frequency-independent conductivity and permeability at the specified frequency and temperature.
Displacement current is neglected. The ratio sigma/(omega epsilon) >= 100 is a conservative catalog screening threshold, not a manufacturer standard.
Skin depth is the field/current amplitude 1/e length, not a hard boundary; power density decays twice as rapidly.
Planar half-space field model; finite wires and proximity effects need additional analysis. No AC resistance or litz-wire performance is inferred.
Use mu0 = 4 pi times 1e-7 H/m and eps0 = 8.8541878128e-12 F/m.

references.title: MIT Center for Bits and Atoms, Circuits, Transmission Lines, and Waveguides, section 7.2.1, equations 7.26–7.35

constraints.message: Conduction must exceed displacement-current admittance by at least 100 for this approximation

title: Mutual and series-connected coupled-coil inductance
description: Predict mutual inductance and both series polarities from two self-inductances and coupling coefficient.
formula: M = k sqrt(L1 L2); Laiding = L1+L2+2M; Lopposing = L1+L2-2M
assumptions: Two passive reciprocal linear coils, with self-inductances measured with the other winding open at the same operating frequency and bias.
Coupling coefficient is a magnitude between 0 and 1; dot convention and wiring determine aiding versus opposing.
No saturation, significant frequency dispersion, winding capacitance or resistive losses. Opposing mode may be dominated by parasitics near perfect coupling.
At k=1 and equal self-inductances the ideal opposing value is zero; this does not imply a real physical winding has zero parasitic inductance.
Separate square roots avoid forming L1*L2; the root-difference term is rationalized as (L1-L2)/(sqrt(L1)+sqrt(L2)) to preserve small unequal-winding mismatch. No clamp is used.

references.title: UC Berkeley EECS-2007-3, section 3.2.2, equations 3.6–3.8: Mutual inductance and coupling coefficient
MIT Electromagnetic Fields and Energy, section 9.7: Linear two-winding flux-linkage matrix

title: Sinusoidal transformer peak flux density
description: Calculate peak core flux density from sinusoidal winding voltage and check a user-supplied material operating limit.
formula: Bpk = sqrt(2) Vrms/(2 pi f N Ae); Phiflux,pk = Bpk Ae
assumptions: Applied winding voltage is sinusoidal, zero-mean, and equal to the induced voltage; no DC flux offset.
Flux is approximately uniform over effective magnetic cross section Ae; winding drops and leakage are neglected.
The exact sinusoidal factor 2 pi/sqrt(2) is used rather than the rounded 4.44.
The supplied flux limit must be appropriate for material, temperature and frequency; satisfying it does not certify acceptable core loss.

references.title: Micrometals Power Conversion and Line Filter Applications, Issue L, printed page 29: Core loss and sinusoidal form factor
MIT 6.014 Lecture 11: Faraday's law and transformer winding voltage

constraints.message: Turns must be a positive integer
Predicted flux exceeds the supplied material operating limit

title: Magnetic field energy in a material volume
description: Find magnetic energy density and stored field energy in a uniform linear-material region, such as an inductor air gap.
formula: u = B²/(2 mu0 mur); W = u Volume
assumptions: Uniform magnetic field in a homogeneous, isotropic, linear material with real constant permeability and no hysteresis.
Only the specified material region is integrated; this is not necessarily total device energy. Use separate regions for a core and its gap.
For an air gap, relative permeability is approximately 1. For nonlinear materials the integral of H dB replaces B²/(2 mu).
The user-supplied field limit defines the chosen linear regime; it must come from appropriate material data. Use mu0 = 4 pi times 1e-7 H/m.

references.title: MIT 6.014 Lecture 11, equations 9 and 15: Magnetic energy density and volume integral
MIT 8.02 Inductance Worked Examples, examples 1 and 3: B²/(2 mu0)

constraints.message: Field exceeds the supplied linear-regime limit
